projects.context:
All 5 concepts were built on the same content and the same product truth. What changed each time was how much of the page carried the argument and how much of it carried the interface. That was the point: give the client a few genuinely different layouts to react to instead of 5 variations of one idea.

Keeping the spine fixed was deliberate. It meant the client was comparing visual language and layout logic each time instead of comparing content, so feedback came back about direction rather than wording.


What changed between them was one decision: how early and how literally the product interface appears, and whether the page's rhythm is carried by the brand or by the software.

projects.story: Specialty coffee roastery in Düsseldorf selling single-origin coffee, equipment and ceramics, running barista and latte art courses and supplying cafés and offices as a wholesale partner. I designed the brand identity and the whole site, then built it on Shopify. The brand work set the b12 wordmark and the Specialty Coffee Roastery emblem, the forest green and cream palette and the Outfit type system, and a UI component library the rest of the site is assembled from. The shop covers the catalogue with filters, product pages for coffee and for merchandise, quick view, cart and search. The coffee school area carries the course range and a single course page, where enrolment runs through a course request that captures the course, the preferred date and the group size, with private event and gift flows as their own modals. The B2B area presents custom roasts, barista training, verified origin reports and equipment advice, with a partnership application and wholesale pricing behind a separate sign-up. Venue and catering, membership, sustainability and the legal pages complete the site, all designed at 1920, 1440, 744 and 360.
projects.context: Coffee roastery with three audiences on one site: retail customers buying beans and ceramics, people booking barista and latte art courses, and cafés and offices applying for wholesale terms. The structure had to let each of the three find their own path without crowding the others.

projects.story: Beauty Label is a Brooklyn hair salon led by Mariana Sidey that calls itself a collective of artists and specialises in luxury blonde colour, extensions and general hair services. The site has to carry two jobs at once, filling the chair and moving retail product, so I designed the booking path as the spine and let the shop sit alongside it instead of competing with it. Appointment booking repeats down the page with a free 30-minute consultation as the low-commitment entry for first-time clients, and the salon retail shelf presents professional lines from Kérastase, Aveda, Moroccanoil and Oribe across new arrivals, tools, shampoo and conditioner, treatments and oils. Stylist profiles, partner brands and testimonials carry the credibility a colour specialist is judged on.
projects.context: A salon that sells appointments and retail product from the same page, where the booking path had to stay dominant while the shop still functioned. Luxury blonde colour is a trust purchase, so stylist profiles, partner brands and reviews carry as much weight as the services list.

German-language site.
projects.context: Services business with no shop and no catalogue, so every section has to move the visitor toward a Beratung anfordern consultation request and the non-binding quote that follows it. projects.context:
Concept 01 = Modern Luxury
This concept focuses on the product and conversion. I restructured the information hierarchy, removed repetitive messaging, unified the UI components, and created a cleaner layout so visitors could quickly understand the value of the Mystery Bourbon Box and move naturally toward the primary CTA. Visually, the direction creates a contemporary, high-end ecommerce experience with the product at its center.
Concept 02 = The Curator’s Journal
This concept shifts the emphasis toward brand storytelling. I reorganized the content flow so visitors first discover Whiskey Library’s philosophy and expertise before being introduced to the product. Editorial layouts, large-scale photography, and a curated archive of previous discoveries replace more conventional product sections. The direction is intended to build trust and position Whiskey Library as an exclusive whiskey club rather than a traditional ecommerce store.
